---
title: Next.js
description: Add ClipMux uploads, playback and webhooks to a Next.js App Router app with one route file and one client component.
---

In Next.js, ClipMux is one route handler and one client component. The
route handler answers the uploader, the player and ClipMux's webhooks; the
component puts the two elements on your page. This is the setup the
[quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart) walks through, with the details
around it.

## Before you start

- A Next.js app with the App Router, on Node 20.19 or later.
- A ClipMux server and its owner to approve your app.
- The packages, and your app connected:

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
npx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
pnpm dlx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## The env file

`init` writes five variables to `.env.local`, which Next.js loads on the
server:

| Variable | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `CLIPMUX_URL` | The ClipMux server's public URL. |
| `CLIPMUX_API_KEY` | Your app's API key, `cmx_…`. |
| `CLIPMUX_SIGNING_KID` | The ID of your app's signing key. |
| `CLIPMUX_SIGNING_KEY` | The signing key itself, a PEM. |
| `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | The webhook secret, `whsec_…`. |

None has the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix, so none reaches the browser. Keep it
that way, and keep `.env.local` out of git. In production, set the same
five in your host's secret settings.

## The route file

<include cwd lang="ts" meta='title="app/api/clipmux/[action]/route.ts"'>snippets/node/nextjs/route.ts</include>

The `[action]` segment makes this one file answer POSTs to
`/api/clipmux/upload`, `/api/clipmux/playback` and
`/api/clipmux/webhook`. `requireInstructor`, `getUser`, `canWatch` and `db`
stand for your own code.

- `upload` runs when someone chooses a file. Return the upload's settings,
  or `null` to refuse with `403`.
- `playback` runs when someone presses play, and again when the token runs
  out. Return `{ viewerId }`, or `null` to refuse.
- `asset` runs for each verified webhook, with the video re-fetched.

A callback you leave out makes its route a `404`. See
[Receive webhooks](/docs/build/webhooks) for `event` and `onError`.

The handler reads the request body itself, so the webhook's raw body
reaches it untouched; there's nothing to configure. It uses only Web APIs,
so the route also runs on the Edge runtime.

## The client component

<include cwd lang="tsx" meta='title="app/lessons/[id]/video.tsx"'>snippets/node/nextjs/video.tsx</include>

`'use client'` and the `import()` inside `useEffect` keep the elements out
of the server render: they need the DOM, and the player needs Media Source.
The two `import type` lines add the elements' JSX types without loading
them.

Render it from a server component, which reads the playback ID from your
database:

```tsx title="app/lessons/[id]/page.tsx"
import { LessonVideo } from './video'

export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = await params
  const lesson = await db.lesson.findUnique({ where: { id } })
  return <LessonVideo lessonId={id} playbackId={lesson?.playbackId ?? undefined} />
}
```

To react when a viewer is refused, handle `clipmux-denied` and call
`router.refresh()` to re-render the page's locked state. See
[Add the player](/docs/build/play/player).

## Content-Security-Policy

If your app sends a Content-Security-Policy, pages with the elements must
allow ClipMux's origins. `doctor` prints them:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node doctor
```

For each directive (`connect-src`, `media-src`, `img-src` and `style-src`), it
names the exact origins your server uses.

Add those sources to the directives your app already sets, in
`next.config.ts` headers or your middleware. `connect-src` also lists the
storage bucket that upload parts go to, when it isn't the ClipMux server.

## Check it works

Run `npx @clipmux/node doctor`; it ends with `✓ Ready.` Then forward
webhooks and upload from the lesson page:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook
```

`listen` prints `✓ video.asset.ready ast_… → 200` when encoding is done,
and the video plays after a reload.

- The uploader shows an error at once: your `upload` callback returned
  `null`, or threw.
- `/api/clipmux/upload` answers with Next.js's own 404 page: the file isn't
  at `app/api/clipmux/[action]/route.ts`.
- `listen` shows `400`: the app reads a different `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
  from the one `listen` signs with.
